title: Advanced Workflows
text: Standard equality blocking misses pairs names spelled differently sound alike — example, “Smith” / “Smyth” “Jon” / “John”. Pass .transform = il_soundex il_block_on() block_on() group names phonetic code instead exact spelling. Use .transform argument specifying blocking rule EM training pass: Phonetic blocking increases recall cost candidate pairs. Use il_count_pairs() check volume trade-committing spec.
code: spec_phon <- il_spec() |>   il_compare(first_name, cl_name()) |>   il_compare(surname, cl_name()) |>   il_compare(dob, cl_dob()) |>   il_block_on(first_name, .transform = il_soundex) |>   il_block_on(surname, .transform = il_soundex) model_phon <- il_model(df, spec = spec_phon, con = con) model_phon <- il_estimate_u(model_phon, max_pairs = 1e5) model_phon <- il_estimate_em(   model_phon,   block_on(first_name, .transform = il_soundex) ) #> EM trained: surname and dob | skipped (blocked on): #> first_name

title: Getting Started
text: Record linkage (also called entity resolution deduplication) task identifying records one datasets refer real-world entity. datasets lack shared unique identifier, must rely imperfect fields like names, dates birth, addresses decide rows belong together. Probabilistic record linkage formalises estimating likelihood two records match given similar across multiple fields. irelink implements Fellegi-Sunter model probabilistic record linkage. Parameters estimated via unsupervised Expectation-Maximization, labeled training data required get started.

title: Getting Started
text: Every linkage task follows general pattern: Define specification — choose columns compare . Build model — load data SQL backend attach specification. Train parameters — estimate u-probabilities, run EM learn m-probabilities. Predict — score every candidate pair threshold get likely matches. Cluster — resolve pairwise links groups records represent entity. example walks step using small built-dataset.

text: rec_id column encodes ground truth. Extract entity IDs build pairwise labels:
code: # Extract entity number from rec_id (e.g., "rec-1070-org" -> "1070") entity_a <- sub('^rec-(\\d+)-org$', '\\1', febrl4a$rec_id) entity_b <- sub('^rec-(\\d+)-dup-\\d+$', '\\1', febrl4b$rec_id)  # Build id-entity lookup (unique_id auto-generated by il_model) ids_a <- data.frame(unique_id = seq_len(nrow(febrl4a)), entity = entity_a) ids_b <- data.frame(unique_id = seq_len(nrow(febrl4b)), entity = entity_b)  # True matches: same entity across tables positives <- merge(ids_a, ids_b, by = 'entity') names(positives) <- c('entity', 'unique_id_l', 'unique_id_r') positives$is_match <- 1L positives <- positives[, c('unique_id_l', 'unique_id_r', 'is_match')]  # Sample non-matching pairs set.seed(42) n_neg <- min(nrow(positives), 2000L) neg_l <- sample(ids_a$unique_id, n_neg, replace = TRUE) neg_r <- sample(ids_b$unique_id, n_neg, replace = TRUE) ent_l <- ids_a$entity[match(neg_l, ids_a$unique_id)] ent_r <- ids_b$entity[match(neg_r, ids_b$unique_id)] negatives <- data.frame(   unique_id_l = neg_l,   unique_id_r = neg_r,   is_match = ifelse(ent_l == ent_r, 1L, 0L) )  labels <- rbind(positives, negatives) nrow(labels) #> [1] 7000 sum(labels$is_match) #> [1] 5001

code: counts <- il_count_pairs(   df_origin,   df_destination,   # Same year-month, similar memo prefix, amount ratio within 30%   block_on(     .where = paste(       "strftime(l.transaction_date, '%Y%m') = strftime(r.transaction_date, '%Y%m')",       'AND substr(l.memo, 1, 3) = substr(r.memo, 1, 3)',       'AND l.amount / r.amount > 0.7 AND l.amount / r.amount < 1.3'     )   ),   # Same but offset by 15 days to catch month boundaries   block_on(     .where = paste(       "strftime(l.transaction_date + 15, '%Y%m') = strftime(r.transaction_date, '%Y%m')",       'AND substr(l.memo, 1, 3) = substr(r.memo, 1, 3)',       'AND l.amount / r.amount > 0.7 AND l.amount / r.amount < 1.3'     )   ),   # title: Fast Probabilistic Record Linkage
text: irelink brings fast, scalable probabilistic record linkage R. implements Fellegi-Sunter model identify link duplicate related records across datasets lack shared unique identifier. Model parameters estimated via unsupervised Expectation-Maximization, labeled training data required. Comparison functions cover exact matching, Jaro-Winkler, Levenshtein, date differences, geographic distance, letting tailor model data. Multiple SQL backends supported DBI, code runs SQLite, DuckDB, PostgreSQL. irelink translation Python splink library idiomatic R.

title: Fast Probabilistic Record Linkage
text: Find duplicate records within single dataset. bundled fake_20 dataset provides small example experimentation. irelink pushes data SQL database efficient pair generation, need DBI connection. use -memory DuckDB instance. il_spec describes linkage model: fields compare, compare , blocking rules apply. Blocking rules restrict record pairs generated. pairs share surname first name scored, keeping computation manageable. il_estimate_u() estimates parameters non-matching pairs via random sampling, il_estimate_em() refines match-weight parameters using Expectation-Maximization. predict() scores candidate pairs returns match-probability threshold. returned match_weight evidence-log2 Bayes factor; total_match_weight adds prior odds used compute match_probability. il_cluster() groups matched pairs deduplicated entities. il_cleanup() drops temporary tables owned model. Use il_cleanup_all(con) interactive escape hatch failed exploratory session may left several irelink models’ tables behind.
code: library(irelink)  df <- fake_20 con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb()) spec <- il_spec() |>   il_compare(first_name, cl_jaro_winkler(0.9, 0.7)) |>   il_compare(surname, cl_jaro_winkler(0.9, 0.7)) |>   il_compare(dob, cl_exact()) |>   il_block_on(surname) |>   il_block_on(first_name)  model <- il_model(df, spec = spec, con = con) model <- il_estimate_u(model) model <- il_estimate_em(model, block_on(surname)) #> EM trained: first_name and dob | skipped (blocked on): surname pairs <- predict(model, threshold = 0.5) clusters <- il_cluster(pairs) clusters #> # A tibble: 18 × 2 #>    unique_id cluster_id #>    <chr>     <chr>      #>  1 10        cluster_10 #>  2 4         cluster_13 #>  3 17        cluster_17 #>  4 3         cluster_13 #>  5 9         cluster_10 #>  6 13        cluster_13 #>  7 7         cluster_17 #>  8 20        cluster_10 #>  9 5         cluster_15 #> 10 15        cluster_15 #> 11 14        cluster_13 #> 12 6         cluster_15 #> 13 8         cluster_17 #> 14 19        cluster_10 #> 15 12        cluster_1  #> 16 11        cluster_1  #> 17 2         cluster_1  #> 18 1         cluster_1 il_cleanup(model) DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
